title: Elodie and the Confession
premise: True-crime podcaster Coral Almeida takes on the thirty-year-old disappearance of heiress Marguerite Vasseur, only for a fresh corpse to surface wearing clothes lifted from Coral's own closet—a message meant to drag Coral's hidden past into the light. As Coral interviews the Vasseur family before their annual anniversary dinner, alibis built three decades ago begin to fray, revealing that Coral's late mother was the housekeeper who vanished the same night. The killer is Marguerite's brother, Auguste, who murdered both women to protect his inheritance and has spent years watching Coral, staging the body to silence the podcast before it exposes him. At the anniversary dinner, Coral turns the toast into a trap, extracting a recorded confession as the family—and the police—listen.
about_author: Noor Joubert is a former archivist from a coastal town who grew up listening to her grandmother's unsolved mysteries over Sunday dinners. She writes slow-burn mysteries about families that keep their secrets beautifully pressed, like linens no one is allowed to use.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case on Record
chapters.summary: Coral Almeida, POV. Coral launches season four of their podcast with the 1994 disappearance of heiress Marguerite Vasseur, priding themselves on a perfect closure record. Researching in an archive, Coral finds their mother's name on the staff roster—unexplained. Emotional beat: confident professionalism cracked by a private tremor.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Police call Coral to a marsh outside the Vasseur estate: a woman dead two days, dressed head-to-toe in garments stolen from Coral's own apartment. The victim is unidentified; the clothes are unmistakably Coral's. Emotional beat: violation—the watcher has been watched.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashback fragments. Coral admits to their producer, Dev, that their mother Solange was the Vasseurs' housekeeper who disappeared the same night as Marguerite—Coral's origin story they've never aired. Emotional beat: shame of a secret kept too long.

chapters.title: Invitation to the Estate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Matriarch Yvonne Vasseur invites Coral to stay through the thirtieth-anniversary dinner, all charm and control. Coral accepts, cataloguing the house: locked east wing, a portrait missing from its frame. Emotional beat: predator-and-prey ambiguity—who invited whom?

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral interviews the siblings: Auguste, smooth and grieving; Camille, brittle with wine; cousin Théo, evasive. Each account of the night Marguerite vanished aligns too perfectly, like rehearsed testimony. Emotional beat: unease at harmony that sounds like conspiracy.

chapters.title: What the Closet Knew
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille privately recognizes the dead woman's shoes as ones she sold at auction years ago, meaning someone tracked provenance meticulously. She says nothing at dinner but leaves an anonymous note under Coral's door. Emotional beat: guilt complicity wearing thin.

chapters.title: Solange's Room
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral breaks into the sealed servants' wing and finds their mother's room preserved: a diary with pages razored out, and a child's drawing signed 'Coral.' Someone has been visiting it recently—fresh footprints in dust. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Dev's POV (podcast segments interwoven). Dev traces the podcast's anonymous tipster, whose emails predate the murder by weeks—the case was baited. The tipster's IP pings near the estate. Emotional beat: dawning horror that Coral was lured, not chosen.

chapters.title: Auguste's Toast
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a pre-dinner reception, Auguste delivers a flawless tribute to Marguerite while watching Coral across the room. He quotes a line from Coral's own podcast, unaired. Emotional beat: terror dressed as civility.

chapters.title: Théo's Debt
chapters.summary: Théo's POV. Théo confesses to the reader he was paid to falsify his 1994 alibi by Auguste, gambling debts long since buried. He drafts a statement to Coral, then burns it when he spots someone in the garden. Emotional beat: cowardice curdling toward courage.

chapters.title: The Missing Portrait
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral identifies the absent portrait: it depicted Solange, not Marguerite. Behind the frame's backing, a hidden compartment yields one surviving diary page—Marguerite had discovered Auguste was forging their mother's will. Emotional beat: motive surfacing like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: Camille Breaks
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Confronted gently by Coral, Camille admits she saw Auguste return soaked and shaking the night of the disappearances, and was bought with her inheritance. She agrees to testify—if she survives the dinner. Emotional beat: relief and dread arriving together.

chapters.title: A Second Body
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Théo is found dead in the boathouse, staged again in clothing connected to Coral—an escalation meant to frame them. Police now eye Coral as suspect. Emotional beat: the trap closing from every side.

chapters.title: Dev Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev arrives unannounced to warn Coral, but their recordings are seized by a lawyer claiming estate privacy. Dev hides a backup drive in the chapel and sends Coral a coded message. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Diary Reassembled
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Matching the razored diary against Marguerite's letters held by the town notary, Coral reconstructs the truth: Marguerite planned to disinherit Auguste and name Solange as witness; both were silenced in one night. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the coldest case runs warm with blood.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Watching
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV, first time. Auguste reflects on raising Coral from afar, funding their career, engineering the podcast invitation—he wanted a confession audience worthy of him. He believes the dinner will be his masterpiece. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy of obsession.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the eve of the dinner, Coral's room is locked from outside, phone jammed, evidence gone. Through the wall, Coral hears Auguste reassuring Yvonne that 'the podcaster won't be a problem after tomorrow.' Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair before defiance.

chapters.title: The Chapel Drive
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev retrieves the backup drive, evades the family lawyer, and slips the evidence to a retired detective who once doubted the 1994 file. The detective agrees to attend the dinner quietly. Emotional beat: hope smuggled in like contraband.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Released for the dinner, Coral raises a glass and toasts not Marguerite but Solange, reciting the reconstructed diary aloud as the detective records. Auguste's composure cracks glass by glass. Emotional beat: the trap inverted—every guest a witness.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV. Cornered by the diary page, Camille's testimony, and the recording, Auguste confesses—not with remorse but with pride, detailing how invisibility was his inheritance too. Police take him as Yvonne collapses. Emotional beat: horror and release entwined.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Air
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral wrestles with airing their mother's story versus honoring her privacy, finally releasing an episode that tells the truth without exploiting it. The case closes; the record does too. Emotional beat: grief given shape and sound.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. A year later, Coral visits the estate turned memorial, places their childhood drawing in Solange's restored room, and receives a letter from an heir thanking them. Loyalty and truth, Coral concludes, were never opposites—only late acquaintances. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
